source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Wheels and Tires, p.10-5

procedures.title: Tires: repair punctures
steps: Repair punctures permanently from inside the tire with it off the wheel; treat outside plug repairs as temporary and fix permanently soon.
Hot patch: clean all debris out of the hole without making it bigger, then vulcanize the patch per its maker's instructions.
Rubber plug: plugs go in from inside, or from outside without dismounting; coat the hole with repair cement first and follow the kit instructions.
Cold (self-vulcanizing) patch: clean the hole without enlarging it, buff an area inside big enough for the patch, then apply the special cement and patch per instructions.
Pressure gun: get materials and instructions from the tire supplier.

procedures.title: Tire installation safety precautions
steps: Make sure the rim flanges and bead ledges, especially hump and radius areas, are clean and smooth; wire-brush (or file, if severe) off old rubber, dried soap, rust and heavy paint.
Coat the beads, flanges and bead ledges generously with thin vegetable oil soap solution or approved rubber lubricant.
Never let pressure exceed 40 pounds while seating beads; if not seated by 40 pounds, deflate, re-center on the rim, re-lubricate and inflate again.
Make sure the valve core is in before inflating.
Use an extension gauge with a clip-on chuck so you can watch pressure while standing well clear.
notes: Building pressure to force a binding bead to seat (dirty, corroded or off-center rim) is DANGEROUS and can burst the bead and injure the mechanic.

procedures.title: Valve assembly: replace
steps: Cut or knock the old valve out of the rim.
Clean the valve hole and the area around it inside the flange with steel wool.
notes: Always fit a new valve assembly.
See figure 6 in the manual for installing the valve.

procedures.title: Wheels: balance
steps: On disc brake cars (Corvette included), take the wheel and tire off the car to balance it, because the spring-loaded pads drag on the disc.
notes: Static (still) balance means weight is evenly spread around the axis of rotation so the wheel has no tendency to turn by itself.
